Hike early morning and carry extra water.

south-kaibab-ooh-aah.note: South Kaibab Trail remains open from the trailhead to the Black Bridge, but the Black Bridge itself is closed along with the rest of the river crossing infrastructure, so the trail effectively ends there with no access across the Colorado River; confirmed today via the National Park Service's Key Hiking Messages page, last updated August 31, 2026 (Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park). This follows a severe flash flood in Bright Angel Canyon on August 29 around 2:30pm that destroyed nearly all footbridges over Bright Angel Creek and required evacuation of 62 people from the Phantom Ranch and lower North Kaibab area; the park states there is no estimated reopening at this time. Additional thunderstorms could bring further flash flooding, debris flows, or rockfall, so conditions could change quickly. This trail is fully sun exposed with no water source below the trailhead; confirm current water status at the trailhead before descending. No NWS Excessive Heat Warning is active for Grand Canyon country today. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

bright-angel-indian-garden.note: Bright Angel Trail remains open only from the trailhead to River Resthouse; hikers should not plan to continue past that point, confirmed today via the National Park Service's Key Hiking Messages page, last updated August 31, 2026 (Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park). This follows a severe flash flood in Bright Angel Canyon on August 29 that closed Phantom Ranch, the North Kaibab Trail, and the river-crossing bridges, destroying nearly all footbridges over Bright Angel Creek and requiring evacuation of 62 people; the park states there is no estimated reopening at this time. Grand Canyon National Park separately advises day hikers descend no farther than 1.5 miles from the upper trailhead due to elevated Inner Canyon heat risk regardless of warning status. Water status at the trailhead and Havasupai Gardens can change suddenly, so verify current conditions before descending. No NWS Excessive Heat Warning is active for Grand Canyon country today. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

rim-trail.note: No closures reported today; the Rim Trail is not affected by the Bright Angel Canyon flash flood closure. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

north-kaibab-coconino.note: North Kaibab Trail, Phantom Ranch, and the Black Bridge and Silver Bridge river crossings remain closed with no estimated reopening, confirmed today via the National Park Service's Key Hiking Messages page, last updated August 31, 2026 (Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park). A severe flash flood struck Bright Angel Canyon around 2:30pm on August 29, destroying nearly all footbridges over Bright Angel Creek and requiring an aerial evacuation of 62 people from the Phantom Ranch and lower North Kaibab area; no injuries were reported. Colorado River traffic through the area, including rafting, is halted. The National Park Service continues to warn that additional thunderstorms could bring further flash flooding, debris flows, and rockfall with little to no warning even when storms are not visible overhead, especially given ongoing Dragon Bravo Fire burn scar hazards. Water status at the North Kaibab Trailhead, Supai Tunnel, and Cottonwood Campground should be considered uncertain until the park posts a post-flood update. No NWS Excessive Heat Warning is active for Grand Canyon country today. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.
